classification.difficultyReason: Construct a turnover model from direct variation, solve two quadratic inequalities and intersect their solution sets to satisfy both business conditions.

content.prompt: A business-owner leases a shop in a shopping centre. There is only one type of product sold by this business.

children.label: a
children.prompt: It is found that the number $n$ of items sold each week varies directly with the difference between $\$84$ and the price $\$p$. That is, when $p=84$ there are no items sold. When the price is $\$60$ there are 192 items sold. Find $n$ as a function of $p$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The turnover $T$ for the product is the number sold times the price. Find $T$ as a function of $p$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}T&=np\\T&=8p(84-p)\\T&=672p-8p^2\end{align*}$$
Here $T$ is the weekly turnover in dollars.

children.label: c
children.prompt: In order to stay in business, the turnover must be at least $\$11\,800$. What price may be charged for the product in order to stay in business?

answer.short:
$25\le p\le59$: prices from $\$25$ to $\$59$, inclusive.

The quadratic is non-positive between its zeroes, 25 and 59.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}8p(84-p)&\ge11800\\p^2-84p+1475&\le0\\(p-25)(p-59)&\le0\end{align*}$$
The zeroes are 25 and 59. Test points $p=0,42,84$ give values $1475,-289,1475$ respectively for $(p-25)(p-59)$. Its sign is therefore positive, negative, positive across the three intervals.

Including the zeroes gives $25\le p\le59$. The price may be from $\$25$ to $\$59$, inclusive.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Because of the business-owner’s lease agreement, if turnover is greater than $\$14\,080$ then extra rent must be paid. What prices can be charged without paying extra rent but still staying in business?

answer.short:
$25\le p\le40$ or $44\le p\le59$.

Intersect the prices giving turnover at most $\$14\,080$ with the interval from part c.
answer.worked:
To avoid extra rent, $T\le14080$.
$$\begin{align*}8p(84-p)&\le14080\\p^2-84p+1760&\ge0\\(p-40)(p-44)&\ge0\end{align*}$$
The zeroes are 40 and 44. Test points $p=0,42,84$ give values $1760,-4,1760$ respectively for $(p-40)(p-44)$. Thus $p\le40$ or $p\ge44$ avoids extra rent.

Intersecting with $25\le p\le59$ from part c gives $25\le p\le40$ or $44\le p\le59$. Prices may be from $\$25$ to $\$40$, or from $\$44$ to $\$59$, with all endpoints included.
